messages.author: 8d1c565878e0e470
messages.subject: CARbayesST models in INLA
parts:
Dear all,

I was originally using the models in package  CARbayesST for spatiotemporal modeling, but due to MCMC convergence issues, I started trying INLA. I'm having some difficulty when implementing the models in package  CARbayesST using INLA, and I can't get 
enough help by searching Google, so I'm here to ask for help.

The first question, I think the Leroux-AR1 model will fit my data well, so I try to describe this model with the following code in inla, but when I apply this INLA model on the example used in the tutorial of the CARbayesST package, the result I get is far different from the MCMC results.
Random effect (from CARbayesST vignette):


formula: f(idarea, model = 'besagproper2', graph = W, group = idtime, control.group=list(model='ar1')

For the second question, I also tried to use the ANOVA model in INLA. The model formula and code are as follows. On the same sample data, the coefficients of the fixed effects of this result are very close to the MCMC results as I expected, but there is a clear difference in WAIC.
Random effect (from CARbayesST vignette):
formula:  f(idtime, model = "besagproper2", graph = D) + f(idarea, model = "besagproper2", graph = W) + f(id, model = "iid")

I'm unsure if these problems are caused by my wrong INLA formula or something else. Can anyone give me some clues?

Thank you very much.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] CARbayesST models in INLA
parts:
Hi,

Inla implements ar(1) as a stationary model, I.e. the marginal variance is constant. The way eq(5) from the other package is written, it looks as if they instead treat the model as having the initial variance equal to the subsequent conditional variances. That is equivalent to having an imagined phi_0 = 0 initial condition instead of a stationary model. If that’s really what they implemented, that might explain differences. Check if the estimated phi values for the first time point seem to be larger (in absolute value) for inla than for the other package.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] CARbayesST models in INLA
parts:
The correct stationary ar(1) model should have variance tau^2/(1-rho_T^2), not tau^2,
So if they implemented it the way their vignette is written, I would say they did it incorrectly. But it might also be just the vignette that’s incorrect, and that the differences you see has some other cause.

Finn
